[spoiler= [b]Seek and Destroy (Hydronia)[/b]]

In Sabrata, there was a new threat, one that Nidal knew all too well. The beasts lurked through the black skies, only outlined by the stars they blotted out on their lumberous, destructive journey. They destroyed city blocks, devastating with no warning. The ravagers were not from the foolish King nor those who proclaimed themselves to be righteous, but from an entirely separate continent from which he called home.

Sitting in the officers hall, he pondered when he would visit his family again. He had to ensure they were safe, but if he left his post it would mean countless others could suffer the same death which he now fears has become of his family. A weary sip of coffee is interrupted by the airbases alarm blasting through the late night air. All squadrons scramble! I repeat, all squadrons! Enemies bearing zero-five-six, flight level four-zero-zero!

The dreary officers hall switched to pandemonium in an instant. Pilots who had fallen asleep shot up half dressed, rushing to equip their flight suits and grab something to keep them awake. Those who had stayed awake like Nidal rushed for the two doors on either side of the building, only slightly avoiding crushing some of the smaller men as they broke out into the cool desert night. Praise be to god that their western-minded king had the thought to try to be at the forefront of technology. The radars he bought from Llyndorra would give them a fighting chance tonight. 

Running across the asphalt of the airstrip, he could see the entire base springing to action. Men in their barracks ran as if their lives depended on it, their destinations being all of vital importance to the success of this mission. Fuel and maintenance trucks raced across the base, holding down their horns to signal that they were coming through and not stopping. A small truck slowed down beside him, just long enough for him to grab onto one of its protruding pieces of equipment and hitch a ride.

Jumping off when getting near his hangar, Nadal would finally see his aircraft tonight. It was one of few the king had managed to purchase from Lavia before the failed coup, a fighter which outmatched anything they fielded before. He still marveled at its design every time he looked at it. He was one of a lucky few. A facts of being a veteran of the Air Volunteer Corps, a decorated fighter pilot, and a fierce dedication to the Generals cause all accumulated in him receiving the highest honor in Sabratas Revolutionary Air Corps, a Bushong Whirlwind. Capable of flying at 580 miles an hour and up to 43,000 feet, all while equipped with four powerful 20mm cannons, it was the only aircraft which could threaten the menace besieging his home.

The technicians hurriedly checked the aircraft and resupplied her with the brass and fuel which would be expended in the skies above. In no time, he was soaring through the black nothingness, climbing ever more to fight an enemy he only knew by a description. Far away, he could see the anti-aircraft guns firing into the stars. They would be assisted by a few mobile guns with radar units on them, even though the guns range itself wasnt adequate to hit these bombers, their radar assisted the bigger ones in getting as close as they could.
As they got to altitude, the squadron would finally show their full hand. Five of their aircraft werent the standard Whirlwinds, they were testbeds, a model the Lavians only kept one of. With their air intakes moved to their sides, the nose was free to house their eyes tonight, a radar with up to three miles of range, forfeiting two of their guns and adding a secondary airman to operate the radar. These would talk to the others on approach, and use their radar to sneak up on the slow and heavy bomber, letting the more heavily armed jets do the majority of the work.

After what felt like an eternity, they would finally find the enemy formation. Using the radars and coordination, they would slip in behind the bombers, being careful to not approach too fast and run their shot. These bombers wouldnt have hit their targets yet, meaning they would only need to land a lucky shot to cause one of these massive bombers to detonate like a powder-keg. Even though he was moments away from attempting to bring them down, he couldnt help but be awestruck at how such a large aircraft could exist, let alone fly. 

A transmission came from the squad lead, nicknamed Tester, to start the attack. Taking the lead, Testers aircraft would roar forward, dropping in altitude before picking a bomber and letting rip with his cannons. The flashes lit up the formation as he strafed the bomber, littering its cockpit with shells and punching a hole in one of its pusher props, causing the engine to catch fire. Before the Hydronians could react to what was happening, the other jets would pick their victims. 

One bomber in the back would have its control surfaces shot off, entering it into a slight dive, unable to recover with the loss of its elevator and rudder. Other bombers would take major and minor damage, but no others would go down. Now that they had made their presence known, it was time for the bombers to respond in kind. Revealing their hidden defences, their remote controlled guns would flip into the open, firing at any jet they thought they saw due to their formation making their targeting radars near useless if the attackers positioned themselves correctly.

For Tester however, this information wouldnt be known. He climbed high, looking for another target to strafe. Catching the attention of a gunner, Testers climb was interrupted by a burst of 20mm cannon fire from a turret, with its aim assisted by a clear radar picture. His plane would have its left wing ripped from the body, sending him spiraling to the ground right in front of Nidals eyes. This loss would only fuel the fury of the squadron, only subsiding after most of its ammunition had been spent. 

They had only gotten away with such a bold attack because it wasnt expected, but not without their own losses. Upon return to base, it would be discovered that two other planes barely made it out, being rendered almost inoperable for the time being. Tester would be listed as Missing In Action. None of them wanted to think that he died, but to hope he managed to bail out somewhere during his planes dramatic spin. 

The Hydronians would be prepared for an attack the next time, but would hopefully be put off by the loss and damage of their precious bombers. The Sabratans would lose three critical aircraft that would be needed for the war to come. In the meantime, the bombers continue. Whether the sorties and AA begin making major impacts or the Hydronians keep turning more civilians against their cause in the attempt to cripple the Sabrati Revolutionary production base remains to be seen.

Losses

Sabrati Revolutionary Air Corps:
1 aircraft destroyed
2 aircraft critically damaged
1 airman declared MIA
1 airman critically injured, died under care

Hydronian Bomber Force:
1 Bomber lost
3 bombers critically damaged
13 airmen declared MIA
8 airmen declared KIA
10 airmen wounded
[/spoiler]

[spoiler= [b]Battlefields and Ambassadors" (Nordiheim)[/b]]

Assembling the fractured groups into one front was stressful enough, now Sahar Arebi had to somehow figure out what to say to this foreign delegation on his doorstep. Nordiheim apparently wanted another scuffle after their own war, and had decided to make that fight. He took a sip from his third cup of tea this morning, trying to keep himself thinking clearly over the evergrowing burden of sleep on his mind. His aid, Ansar, would put forward a question as Sahar paced the local government office which had been turned into their new governments headquarters. Why not accept their help? We need all the armor and experienced men we can get.

Rubbing his head, Sahar would respond. We dont know what they will want in trade for this. Not to mention it could ruin our chances of potential negotiations with the royals to establish something similar to what the Lavians have. Amsar looked exasperated, throwing his hat against the table in frustration. They want to give us equipment! Tanks! Guns! Hell they are sending their own men! There wont be any negotiations if those revolutionaries win, remember that Sahar.

Why is this so important for me to agree with? Shahar would snap back at him. The majority here agree with you, so why must I sign off on it? A long pause would interrupt the conversation, each man staring at the other. After sighing, Amsar spoke. You are the one the people look to. You may not be the highest in the chain, but you are the one everyone trusts. You signing off on this could perhaps improve how people feel about this, and prevent us fracturing. You already worked hard enough on bringing everyone together, we dont need to fall apart.

This hung hard on Shahars mind. The foreign troops could reinvigorate his forces, giving them actual training. On the other hand, this would give them major leverage over his government. Then again, they wouldnt have a government if the revolutionaries won.

Fine. Ill sign off on the agreement. We must use them to reach the Hydronians though. We cant afford to visit far away foreign capitals simply for the chance of intervention as of now, but they can influence him to meet us closer. With that, Amsar left, to inform the others of the sign off. It was time for him to try to manage a third front in this war, diplomacy.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler= [b]The Lavian Response[/b] (short bc I have to wake up at 4am tomorrow)]

The ULR, as young as its democratic government was, responded quickly to the issue on its borders which had just flamed up. Military forces, mainly army and airforce, were positioned in the Sabrati and Ijesa lands. Reaching out to the dug in king and royal government, the Lavians established communications and assured the King he would be accepted into Lavia if he needed to flee. More communications were sent out to the various democratic factions before they coalesced.

The main fear at this stage was border thieves and rogue military units attempting to cross into Ijesa, but the long term concern was the Revolutionary party. The ULR and earlier Greater Lavia was a big influence on the westernization of the nation, the main cause for this civil conflict. If the revolutionaries won, they could be a dangerous neighbor and blame the fast-tracked modernization on them. [/spoiler]
